title: City West: the dunes town that meant to rival Chicago

sources.what: 'City West was founded in 1836'; plat recorded by J. Bigelow, about 25 blocks; at 'the mouth of Fort Creek' near 'Petite Fort', later part of the dunes park; 'nearly forty buildings'/'forty houses' (Ball says 16-20 households, so no count is given); a saw mill 'erected in 1835'; a lake pier 'extending several hundred feet into Lake Michigan'; three hotels named (Bigelow, 30 rooms; Bradley; Morse) (Ball and Bowers also name several hotels, so the short says 'a big hotel' and gives no count); Daniel Webster stopped at the Bigelow on a stagecoach trip west; promoters got $5,000 for a lighthouse that was never built; City West 'was the first to go down under the reaction' of the panic; within a few years the site returned to wilderness; headline: 'Once Rivals of Chicago'.
sources.who: The Vidette-Messenger (Valparaiso), Porter County Centennial edition, Aug. 18, 1936, sec. 1 p. 12, 'City West and Indiana City, Now Gone and Almost Forgotten Were Once Rivals of Chicago' (transcribed by inportercounty.org)

sources.what: The Central House Hotel in Chesterton was originally in City West, 'southwest of the present day pavilion at the Indiana Dunes State Park'; built in 1836; moved to Chesterton 'on skids pulled by oxen teams over snow by David Hopkins in 1850'; 'In 1854, all of the remaining structures in City West were destroyed by a fire' (the caption says an electrical storm caused it; one source, so no cause is given).
sources.who: Steven R. Shook, caption for a Central House Hotel postcard, Historical Images of Porter County (inportercounty.org)

sources.what: Chicago, Indiana City, City West and Michigan City 'all started ... with the hope of becoming large, lake shore cities'; 1837 soundings found a better natural harbor there than at Michigan City.
sources.who: T. H. Ball, Northwestern Indiana from 1800 to 1900 (1900), ch. 20 (transcribed by inportercounty.org)

sources.what: 'By-passed by Congress, City West lost its reason for existence and soon died out.'
sources.who: Martin Zimmerman, The Vidette-Messenger, March 6, 1976 (Porter County Museum)

sources.what: 'No evidence today exists of City West, which was located very near today's beach pavilion at the Indiana Dunes State Park.'
sources.who: John O. Bowers, 'Dream Cities of the Calumet' (1929), with inportercounty.org's note

sources.what: A 19th-century 'dream city' that almost rivaled Chicago; in 1837 it 'tried to knock the Windy City out of the running'.

'About the year, 1836, City West sprang into notice'; 'two capitalists from the East'; 'the national appropriations were long withheld'; fires left on the hearths 'lit up the lake with a conflagration. Soon all was destroyed. Some years after, a pier was built' (so no pier is drawn for the living town); the glass of the darkened windows crushed.
sources.who: Hubert Skinner, Complete History of Porter County (Valparaiso Messenger, 1878), per the fact-check

sources.what: 'About 1836, City West was started'; 'The Central House was moved by Mr. Hopkins from City West about thirty years ago' (among Chesterton's inns).
sources.who: Goodspeed & Blanchard, Counties of Porter and Lake, Indiana (1882), ch. V, per the fact-check

sources.what: 'In the year 1836 four men' began it, 'adventurers in the better sense of that word'; at the mouth of Fort Creek, about ten miles west of Michigan City, to compete with Chicago and Michigan City; 'a large building ... for a store and warehouse'; 'hotels were built', 'the large Exchange hotel'; Daniel Webster, in a two-horse carriage off the stage road, had breakfast at the Morse house; 'The financial crash of 1837'; 'Congress made no appropriation for a harbor'; 'in 1839 few if any were left', the houses empty in 1840; later 'a fire had swept over it and ... all the houses had gone into ashes' (Ball's family lived there).
sources.who: T. H. Ball, Northwestern Indiana from 1800 to 1900 (1900), per the fact-check

sources.what: Promoters Jacob Bigelow, Leverett Bradley, Joshua Hobart and William Morse; surveying fall 1836-spring 1837, main plat dated July 12, 1837; hoped it 'would surpass Chicago'; Morse dammed the creek and built a sawmill; a large store and warehouse; the Exchange, 'the largest tavern in all that region', and smaller hotels; Webster, July 4, 1837 (quoting a Chesterton Tribune editor); 'In 1838 all were gone'; Congress funded Michigan City's harbor instead; 'swept out of existence by a fire'; 'No one saw the conflagration, or knew of it at the time'; one building moved to Chesterton in 1850 by a man named Hopkins, later the Central Hotel (Chesterton Tribune, 1908); the site 'now known as Waverly Beach', 'the last vestige ... has long been obliterated'.
sources.who: John O. Bowers, 'Dream Cities of the Calumet' (1929), per the fact-check

sourcing_note: Told as a vanished town, not a ghost story: no source tells one. Counts disagree (forty buildings vs 16-20 households; three hotels vs several), so the short gives none. The plat date disagrees (1836 vs 1837), so it isn't given; the founding year 1836 is in every source. Webster's visit is in the 1936 Vidette-Messenger, Ball (1900) and Bowers (1929, quoting a Chesterton Tribune editor), but they differ on the house and the vehicle, so neither is given and no stagecoach is drawn. The fire has two sources (Ball; Bowers, who says no one saw it), but its year and cause disagree, so neither is given. The oxen and snow of the move to Chesterton are Shook's alone, so the narration just says hauled off. The pictures are generic: no image of City West is known. Blind independent check Nov. 16: 9 fixes, all made. 'Speculators' became 'promoters' (no source says speculators); the pier is gone from the narration and the pictures (Skinner says it was built 'some years after' the town was destroyed); 'a hotel' became 'a store and a big hotel' (there were several hotels); the stagecoach is gone (Ball: a two-horse carriage; the Vidette: a stagecoach); the Chesterton line now says one of its buildings was hauled there years later and became a hotel (Goodspeed 1882; the Chesterton Tribune via Bowers: 1850); the 1854 smell and glow are out (not in Skinner; Wikipedia's sentence has no footnote, and Bowers says no one saw the fire), and so are the fire's year and cause (sources give 1838, about 1854 and about 1853; a forest fire, travelers' fires or lightning); the watching cabin is gone; credits now name the old histories, not Wikipedia.

beats.text: It was meant to rival Chicago. Now it's gone. City West, Indiana, 1836.
beats.label: PORTER COUNTY, INDIANA
beats.credit: T. H. Ball, 1900; John O. Bowers, 1929; Hubert Skinner, 1878

beats.text: Promoters laid it out at the mouth of Fort Creek, in the dunes west of Michigan City.
beats.label: THE MOUTH OF FORT CREEK
beats.credit: T. H. Ball, 1900; John O. Bowers, 1929; Vidette-Messenger, 1936

beats.text: It had a sawmill, a store and a big hotel. Even Daniel Webster stopped there.
beats.credit: T. H. Ball, 1900; John O. Bowers, 1929

beats.text: Then came the Panic of 1837. The harbor money it was counting on never came.
beats.credit: T. H. Ball, 1900; John O. Bowers, 1929; Hubert Skinner, 1878

beats.text: Within a few years, the town was empty. Years later, one of its buildings was hauled off to Chesterton and became a hotel.
beats.label: WITHIN A FEW YEARS
beats.credit: T. H. Ball, 1900; Goodspeed & Blanchard, 1882; Bowers, 1929

beats.text: A fire swept through and burned what was left of City West.
beats.credit: T. H. Ball, 1900; John O. Bowers, 1929; Hubert Skinner, 1878

beats.text: Today the spot is part of Indiana Dunes State Park, near the beach. Nothing of the town is left.
beats.label: INDIANA DUNES STATE PARK

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.
